20261103AK85116.description: Alaska Measure 3. Prohibits noncitizens from voting.
20261103AK85116.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit noncitizens from voting in any election.

20261103AK85135.description: Alaska Measure 2. Repeals open primaries and ranked choice voting.
20261103AK85135.summary: This ballot measure would repeal the use of open primaries and ranked choice voting in elections, instead returning to party primaries and single-choice general elections.

20261103AL84983.description: Alabama Amendment 4. Requires The Star-Spangled Banner to be played in schools.
20261103AL84983.summary: This proposed amendment to Alabama's constitution would require the national anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner, to be played in schools at least once a week.
20261103AL84983.seatName: 4 - Require The Star-Spangled Banner in public schools

20261103AL84984.description: Alabama Amendment 3. Requires the Pledge of Allegiance in schools and authorizes student prayer.
20261103AL84984.summary: This proposed amendment to Alabama's constitution would require schools to begin the day with the Pledge of Allegiance to the U.S. flag and allow students to lead prayers. Students could opt out of participating.
20261103AL84984.seatName: 3 - Allow student-led prayer and require the Pledge of Allegiance

20261103AR84781.description: Arkansas Issue 1. Declares that only citizens can vote in state and local elections.
20261103AR84781.summary: This proposed amendment to Arkansas' constitution would declare that only citizens may vote in state and local elections.

20261103AR84784.description: Arkansas Issue 2. Declares the right to keep and bear arms to be a fundamental right.
20261103AR84784.summary: This proposed amendment to Arkansas' constitution would declare that the right to keep and bear arms is a fundamental right that also covers ammunition and firearms accessories and components.

20261103AZ84698.description: Arizona Proposition 316. Limits local sales taxes on food.
20261103AZ84698.summary: This ballot measure would cap local sales taxes on food at 2%, subject new or increased food sales taxes to voter approval, and prohibit them from taking effect before June 30, 2027.

20261103AZ84699.description: Arizona Proposition 317. Declares drug cartels to be terrorist organizations.
20261103AZ84699.summary: This ballot measure would declare that drug cartels are terrorist organizations and direct the Arizona Department of Homeland Security to address their threat.

20261103AZ84700.description: Arizona Proposition 144. Requires proof of identity to vote and prohibits noncitizens from voting.
20261103AZ84700.summary: This proposed amendment to Arizona's constitution would prohibit noncitizens from voting, require government-issued proof of identity to vote and bar foreign contributions and expenditures in elections.
20261103AZ84700.seatName: 144 - Require voter ID and citizenship to vote

20261103AZ84701.description: Arizona Proposition 142. Expands prohibition on preferential treatment based on race or ethnicity.
20261103AZ84701.summary: This proposed amendment to Arizona's constitution would expand prohibitions on preferential treatment based on race or ethnicity for state agencies and higher education institutions, including mandatory statements in support of race-based diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.
20261103AZ84701.seatName: 142 - Prohibit race-based preferential treatment or discrimination

20261103AZ84702.description: Arizona Proposition 319. Restricts use of traffic enforcement cameras.
20261103AZ84702.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit new contracts for camera license plate readers to enforce traffic laws starting in 2027 and require approval from local voters to continue existing arrangements.
20261103AZ84702.seatName: 319 - Prohibit traffic photo enforcement systems without voter approval

20261103AZ84713.description: Arizona Proposition 318. Expands restriction on transgender athletes in school sports.
20261103AZ84713.summary: This ballot measure would expand an existing prohibition on male athletes participating on female school sports teams, add restrictions on locker rooms and define a person's sex according to what was listed on an original birth certificate.
20261103AZ84713.seatName: 318 - Require school facility access based on sex assigned at birth

20261103CA84435.description: California Proposition 5. Changes the process for recalling and replacing elected officials.
20261103CA84435.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would change the way replacements are selected when someone is recalled from office by voters. Vacancies would be filled by succession, appointment or special election rather than by electing a new official simultaneously with the recall vote.
20261103CA84435.seatName: 5 - Require separate election for recalled officials

20261103CA84436.description: California Proposition 37. Authorizes $25 billion of bonds for loans to middle-income buyers of new homes.
20261103CA84436.summary: This ballot measure would authorize $25 billion of state bonds to finance loans to purchasers of new homes whose family income is no more than twice the median for the area.

20261103CA84438.description: California Proposition 39. Requires government-issued identification to vote.
20261103CA84438.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would require voters to provide government-issued identification to cast a ballot in person or the last four digits of a government-issued identification number to cast a mail-in ballot.

20261103CA84439.description: California Proposition 40. Imposes a 5% tax on those whose wealth is over $1 billion.
20261103CA84439.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would impose a one-time 5% tax on individuals and trusts with wealth over $1 billion, with revenue to go toward healthcare, food assistance and education. Revenue from the tax would be exempt from state spending limits.
20261103CA84439.seatName: 40 - Impose one-time wealth tax over $1 billion

20261103CA84440.description: California Proposition 41. Requires audits of tax programs and subjects new taxes to spending limits.
20261103CA84440.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would require preelection audits for initiatives proposing special taxes and additional audits every four years. It also would prohibit new tax revenue from being exempted from state spending limits.
20261103CA84440.seatName: 41 - Require audit of programs funded by special taxes

20261103CA84441.description: California Proposition 42. Prohibits taxes on personal savings, assets and retirement holdings.
20261103CA84441.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets and retirement holdings.
20261103CA84441.seatName: 42 - Prohibit new state taxes on personal property

20261103CO84939.description: Colorado Amendment 81. Requires law officers to notify federal immigration authorities of people charged with violent crimes.
20261103CO84939.summary: This proposed amendment to Colorado's constitution would require law enforcement officers to notify the U.S. Department of Homeland Security when charging people with violent crimes or, for those with prior felonies, any crime if they may be in the U.S. illegally.
20261103CO84939.seatName: 81 - Require law enforcement to coordinate with DHS regarding immigration status

20261103CO84941.description: Colorado Proposition 132. Increases penalties for fentanyl crimes.
20261103CO84941.summary: This ballot measure would increase criminal penalties for the possession, manufacture and sale of fentanyl.

20261103CO84944.description: Colorado Proposition 135. Bars surgeries that alter a minor's sex characteristics.
20261103CO84944.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit surgeries to alter a minor's sex characteristics in response to the child's perceived gender or sex. It also would prohibit state funding for such surgeries.

20261103CO84945.description: Colorado Proposition 134. Limits transgender athletes in school sports.
20261103CO84945.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit people with male reproductive systems from participating on female athletic teams at schools.
20261103CO84945.seatName: 134 - Require school sports participation based on biological sex

20261103CO85020.description: Colorado Amendment 82. Creates a right to use natural gas in homes and businesses.
20261103CO85020.summary: This proposed amendment to Colorado's constitution would create a right to use natural gas for cooking and heating in homes and businesses.
20261103CO85020.seatName: 82 - Establish right to purchase and sell natural gas

20261103ID84504.description: Idaho Amendment HJR 6. Makes English the official language.
20261103ID84504.summary: This proposed amendment to Idaho's constitution would make English the official state language, requiring it to be used in all public proceedings, documents, instruction and actions.
20261103ID84504.seatName: HJR 6 - Establish English as official state language

20261103ID84505.description: Idaho Amendment HJR 4. Prohibits citizen-initiated laws on marijuana.
20261103ID84505.summary: This proposed amendment to Idaho's constitution would declare that only the legislature has the power to legalize marijuana, narcotics or other psychoactive drugs, meaning that it cannot be done through citizen initiatives.
20261103ID84505.seatName: HJR 4 - Prohibit drug legalization through initiatives

20261103ID84656.description: Idaho Proposition 1. Allows abortion up to fetal viability.
20261103ID84656.summary: This ballot measure would create a right to make personal reproductive healthcare decisions, including on contraception, fertility treatments and abortion up to fetal viability.

20261103KS85030.description: Kansas Constitutional Amendment 1. Prohibits noncitizens from voting.
20261103KS85030.summary: This proposed amendment to Kansas' constitution would prohibit noncitizens from voting in elections.

20261103KY84590.description: Kentucky Amendment 1. Bars gubernatorial pardons and commutations near elections.
20261103KY84590.summary: This proposed amendment to Kentucky's constitution would prohibit the governor from issuing pardons or commuting sentences during a period beginning 60 days before a gubernatorial election until five weeks after it.
20261103KY84590.seatName: 1 - Limit governor's pardon and commutation power

20261103LA85005.description: Louisiana Amendment 4. Revises gubernatorial term limits.
20261103LA85005.summary: This proposed amendment to Louisiana's constitution would limit governors to serving two total terms, instead of two consecutive terms.

20261103MA85146.description: Massachusetts Question 3. Replaces party primaries with an open primary for the top two candidates.
20261103MA85146.summary: This ballot measure would eliminate separate party primaries and adopt an open primary in which the top two vote recipients advance to the general election. It also would require candidates for governor to be paired with a candidate for lieutenant governor in the primary.

20261103MA85147.description: Massachusetts Question 4. Allows voter registration on Election Day.
20261103MA85147.summary: This ballot measure would allow people to register to vote at polling places on Election Day and repeal a requirement to register at least 10 days before an election.

20261103MA85151.description: Massachusetts Question 8. Repeals the legalization of marijuana for recreational purposes.
20261103MA85151.summary: This ballot measure would repeal laws allowing the legal sale of marijuana for recreational purposes but impose no criminal penalties for possession of less than two ounces. Medical marijuana would remain legal.

20261103MA85152.description: Massachusetts Question 9. Asks voters whether to keep or repeal gun control measures passed in 2024.
20261103MA85152.summary: This referendum asks voters whether to uphold or repeal a 2024 law that expands restrictions on "assault-style" firearms, prohibits "ghost guns" lacking serial numbers, creates an electronic firearm registration system and expands a "red flag" law allowing the temporary removal of guns from people deemed a danger to themselves or others.

20261103MD84884.description: Maryland Question 3. Relaxes restraints on congressional redistricting.
20261103MD84884.summary: This proposed amendment to Maryland's constitution would lift restraints on congressional redistricting. It would apply requirements for compact districts that respect "natural boundaries" only to state legislative districts, not congressional districts.
20261103MD84884.seatName: 3 - Clarify that state redistricting requirements apply only to state legislative districts

20261103MO85027.description: Missouri Amendment 3. Restricts abortion and transgender healthcare for minors.
20261103MO85027.summary: This proposed amendment to Missouri's constitution would repeal a right to abortion until fetal viability and instead allow abortion only in cases of medical emergency or fetal anomaly, or rape or incest up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. It also would ban gender-transition treatments and surgeries for minors.
20261103MO85027.seatName: 3 - Repeal right to abortion and prohibit gender transition for minors

20261103MO85153.description: Missouri Proposition A. Adopts revised U.S. House districts approved by state lawmakers in 2025.
20261103MO85153.summary: This referendum initiative asks Missouri voters whether to adopt new U.S. House districts passed by state lawmakers in 2025.
20261103MO85153.seatName: A - Referendum on the 2025 congressional redistricting map

20261103NC84445.description: North Carolina Voter ID Amendment. Requires photo identification to vote by any method.
20261103NC84445.summary: This proposed amendment to North Carolina's constitution would require photo identification to vote by any method, instead of only when voting in person.

20261103ND84788.description: North Dakota Amendment 1. Requires 60% support from voters to approve constitutional amendments.
20261103ND84788.summary: This proposed amendment to North Dakota's constitution would require 60% support from voters to approve future constitutional amendments.

20261103ND84789.description: North Dakota Amendment 2. Requires public schools to provide free breakfast and lunch.
20261103ND84789.summary: This proposed amendment to North Dakota's constitution would require public schools to provide free breakfast and lunch to all students.

20261103NE84644.description: Nebraska Amendment 1. Extends term limits for state lawmakers.
20261103NE84644.summary: This proposed amendment to Nebraska's constitution would allow state lawmakers to serve three consecutive terms, instead of two, before having to leave office for at least one term.

20261103NV84646.description: Nevada Question 6. Creates a right to abortion until fetal viability.
20261103NV84646.summary: This proposed amendment to Nevada's constitution would create a right to an abortion until fetal viability, or when needed to protect the life or health of the pregnant woman.

20261103NV84647.description: Nevada Question 7. Requires government-issued identification to vote.
20261103NV84647.summary: This proposed amendment to Nevada's constitution would require people to show government-issued photo identification to vote in person, or include the last four digits of a government-issued identification number to vote by mail.

20261103OH84503.description: Ohio Issue 3. Requires government-issued identification to vote.
20261103OH84503.summary: This proposed amendment to Ohio's constitution would require a government-issued photo identification to vote in person, with an exception for religious beliefs. It would require those voting by other means to provide either a photo ID or a government-issued identification number.

20261103OK85119.description: Oklahoma Question 845. Revises criteria and term limits for the Judicial Nominating Commission.
20261103OK85119.summary: This proposed amendment to Oklahoma's constitution would lengthen the term limits for members of the Judicial Nominating Commission and revise criteria for appointments.

20261103SD84879.description: South Dakota Amendment I. Ends an adult Medicaid expansion program if federal funding is reduced.
20261103SD84879.summary: This proposed amendment to South Dakota's constitution would end a Medicaid expansion program for lower-income adults if the federal funding share is reduced below 90%.
20261103SD84879.seatName: I - Medicaid expansion contingent on federal funding

20261103SD84880.description: South Dakota Amendment J. Prohibits noncitizens from voting in elections.
20261103SD84880.summary: This proposed amendment to South Dakota's constitution would prohibit noncitizens from voting in elections.

20261103SD84883.description: South Dakota Amendment L. Requires 60% support from voters to approve constitutional amendments.
20261103SD84883.summary: This proposed amendment to South Dakota's constitution would require 60% support from voters to approve future constitutional amendments.
20261103SD84883.seatName: L - Raise approval threshold for ballot amendments

20261103TN85025.description: Tennessee Amendment 2. Prohibits the state from imposing property taxes.
20261103TN85025.summary: This proposed amendment to Tennessee's constitution would prohibit the state from imposing property taxes.

20261103TN85026.description: Tennessee Amendment 3. Expands crime victims' rights.
20261103TN85026.summary: This proposed amendment to Tennessee's constitution would expand existing rights for crime victims, including the rights to be informed of and heard at court and parole proceedings.

20261103VA84986.description: Virginia Question 1. Creates a right to abortion.
20261103VA84986.summary: This proposed amendment to Virginia's constitution would create reproductive rights, including the right to abortion, contraception and fertility care. Abortion could be regulated in the third trimester, but would have to be allowed to protect the life or health of the pregnant woman or when the fetus is not viable.

20261103VA84987.description: Virginia Question 3. Restores voting rights of felons upon release from prison.
20261103VA84987.summary: This proposed amendment to Virginia's constitution would create a fundamental right to vote and would restore the suspended voting rights of convicted felons upon their release from incarceration.

20261103VA84988.description: Virginia Question 2. Repeals a provision limiting marriage to one man and one woman.
20261103VA84988.summary: This proposed amendment to Virginia's constitution would repeal a limitation on marriage to one man and one woman and instead declare that two adults cannot be denied marriage based on sex, gender or race.

20261103VT85083.description: Vermont Proposal 3. Creates a right to form labor unions for collective bargaining.
20261103VT85083.summary: This proposed amendment to Vermont's constitution would create a right to form labor unions for collective bargaining with employers on wages, hours, working conditions and other items.

20261103VT85084.description: Vermont Proposal 4. Adds an equal protection clause to people's constitutional rights.
20261103VT85084.summary: This proposed amendment to Vermont's constitution would guarantee equal treatment based on race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and national origin.

20261103WA85158.description: Washington Initiative 1. Restores a school parental rights law.
20261103WA85158.summary: This ballot measure would restore a school parental rights law to the version originally passed in 2024, including parents' rights to prior notification about medical services and to review their child's school records within 10 business days of a request.

20261103WA85159.description: Washington Initiative 638. Bars biological males from competing in school sports for females.
20261103WA85159.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit biological males from competing in school sports reserved for females and require students to provide a signed statement from a healthcare provider verifying their biological sex based on reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or natural testosterone levels.
20261103WA85159.seatName: 638 - Require school sports participation based on biological sex

20261103WA85160.description: Washington Initiative 645. Repeals a state income tax on millionaires.
20261103WA85160.summary: This ballot measure would repeal a 9.9% state tax on individual income over $1 million.

20261103WI85106.description: Wisconsin Question 2. Prohibits ordering the closure of places of worship during declared emergencies.
20261103WI85106.summary: This proposed amendment to Wisconsin's constitution would prohibit state and local governments from ordering the closure of places of worship in response to a state of emergency, including a public health emergency.
20261103WI85106.seatName: 2 - Prohibit the closure of places of worship during emergencies

20261103WI85108.description: Wisconsin Question 3. Prohibits discrimination or preferential treatment based on race or sex.
20261103WI85108.summary: This proposed amendment to Wisconsin's constitution would prohibit governmental entities, public schools and higher education institutions from discriminating or granting preferential treatment on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin.
20261103WI85108.seatName: 3 - Prohibit governmental entities from discriminating or granting preferential treatment

20261103WV84796.description: West Virginia Amendment 1. Prohibits noncitizens from voting in elections.
20261103WV84796.summary: This proposed amendment to West Virginia's constitution would declare that only citizens may vote in elections.
